findings_informational.title: optuna_search.py PF floor tuning now silently ineffective
findings_informational.detail: optuna_search.py:50 searches over PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR (old alias), and apply_trial_config patches the alias via unittest.mock.patch. Since the new code reads PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR_EVOLUTION and PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR_ADMISSION directly, patching the alias has zero effect on actual behavior. Optuna trials will appear to run but won't actually tune the PF floor value. This is out of scope per the task spec (which limits changes to 5 target files), but should be addressed in a follow-up: either split the Optuna search space into two parameters or update apply_trial_config to patch both new flags.

findings_informational.title: Existing tests monkeypatching old alias now test different behavior
findings_informational.detail: Seven existing tests in test_phase2_rule_pool.py and test_phase2_support.py monkeypatch `PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR` (old name) to 0.0 or 2.0. Since the code now reads PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR_EVOLUTION (default 1.05) and PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR_ADMISSION (default 1.15) directly, these monkeypatches are silently ineffective on the new flags. The tests continue to pass because the EVOLUTION default of 1.05 is low enough that most test PF values (e.g., 1.2) pass, or the penalty differences are still directional. Example: test_pf_floor_still_penalizes_support (line 2190) intends floor=2.0 with penalty=7.5 but gets EVOLUTION=1.05 with penalty=2.75; assertion still holds but for different reasons. This is not a correctness issue today but creates brittleness — changing the EVOLUTION default or test PF values could break these tests silently. Consider a future cleanup to rename these monkeypatches to PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR_EVOLUTION or PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR_ADMISSION as appropriate.

summary: Code review PASSES. The implementation is surgically precise: the single PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR is correctly split into EVOLUTION (1.05, soft penalty) and ADMISSION (1.15, hard gate) with a clean deprecated alias. No blocking, high, or medium issues found — the runtime behavior change is correct and well-tested.
